questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Each of the students __________ completed their assignments.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**has**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject "**Each of the students**" is singular, so the verb must also be singular.
 
• "**Has**" is the correct singular auxiliary verb to match the singular subject "Each."
 
• Other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Will** indicates future tense, but the context suggests present perfect.
 
• **Were** and **are** are plural forms and do not agree with the singular subject "Each."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Each of the students **has**__ completed their assignments."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Each"** always takes a singular verb, regardless of the plural noun that follows.
 
• Example: "Each of the players **has** a unique skill set."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence and rectify it. If no correction is needed, select 'No correction required'.

The cake (was baking) in the oven when I arrived.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb phrase "**was baking**" incorrectly suggests that the cake was actively baking itself, which is illogical since the cake is the object being baked, not the doer of the action.
 
• The sentence requires a **passive construction** because the cake is undergoing the baking process.
 
• "**Was being baked**" correctly conveys that the cake was in the process of being baked at the time of arrival.
 
• Other options do not fit the continuous action in the past passive: 
 
 
• **Was baked:** Simple past passive, indicates completed action.
 
• **Baked:** Simple past active, incorrect without a subject performing the action.
 
• **No correction required:** Incorrect, as the original phrase is grammatically flawed.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The cake **was being baked** in the oven when I arrived."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In passive voice, use forms like "is being," "was being," or "has been" + past participle to indicate the action done to the subject.
 
• Example: "The book was being read by the student."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The _________ design of the new energy-efficient appliances has reduced electricity consumption significantly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**innovative**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank precedes the noun "**design**," so an adjective is required to describe the design.
 
• "**Innovative**" is the adjective form of "innovation" and correctly describes the design.
 
• Other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Innovativeness:** A noun meaning the quality of being innovative, not suitable before a noun like "design."
 
• **Innovation:** A noun meaning the act of innovating, not appropriate as an adjective.
 
• **Innovates:** A verb form, completely incorrect in this context.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The **innovative**__ design of the new energy-efficient appliances has reduced electricity consumption significantly."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Adjectives modify nouns and fit before them to describe their qualities.
 
• Example: "The **modern** architecture attracted many visitors."

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with an adverbial usage error.

Mr. Joe remarked / that the audience / brightly listened / to the speech.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adverb "**brightly**" refers to light or a cheerful expression and is not suitable for describing how someone **listens**.
 
• The correct adverb should describe the manner of listening. Suitable alternatives could be "**attentively**", "**carefully**", or "**quietly**."
 
• The error is in the segment "**brightly listened**" as "brightly" is incorrectly modifying the verb "listened."
 
• Other parts of the sentence are grammatically correct and do not contain adverbial usage errors.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Mr. Joe remarked that the audience **attentively listened** to the speech."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Brightly**" is typically used for describing expressions ("She smiled brightly") or light ("The sun shone brightly").
 
• Verbs like "listen" require adverbs that relate to mental focus or manner, e.g., "carefully," "closely," "attentively."

questions.question:
Select the word that best completes the given sentence. Determine the collocation through the sentence.

Deepa is ___________ worried about you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**deeply**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb phrase "**worried about**" commonly collocates with the adverb "**deeply**" to express strong emotional concern.
 
• "**Deeply worried**" is a standard and natural collocation in English to convey serious concern or anxiety.
 
• Other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Sadly:** Refers to sorrow, not worry, and does not collocate with "worried."
 
• **Brightly:** Refers to light or cheerfulness, unrelated to worry.
 
• **Gracefully:** Describes physical movement or manner, not emotions like worry.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Deepa is **deeply**__ worried about you."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Common collocations with "deeply" include: "deeply concerned," "deeply regret," "deeply grateful," and "deeply affected."
 
• These expressions convey strong or profound emotional states.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Last week, while walking in the garden, I saw a toddler who was sleeping in the pram.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**while walking in the garden**" creates ambiguity about who was walking — the speaker or the toddler.
 
• Grammatically, the modifier "**while walking in the garden**" should refer to the subject of the main clause, which is "**I**," but the sentence structure places "I saw a toddler who was sleeping," which causes confusion.
 
• To remove the ambiguity, it should be rephrased as "**While I was walking in the garden**."
 
• The rest of the sentence is grammatically correct and clear.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Last week, while **I was walking in the garden**, I saw a toddler who was sleeping in the pram."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dangling participles like "while walking" can confuse the reader if it is unclear who is performing the action.
 
• Clear and explicit subjects avoid such ambiguities in complex sentences.
